title: Gerbner et al.'s hemi-bundled Bollobás conjecture for intersecting families
literal_statement:
Let $AK(n,k,t)$ denote the maximum size of a $k$-uniform $t$-intersecting family $F\subseteq {[n]\choose k}$. Let $\{(A_i,B_i)\}_{i=1}^m$ be a collection of pairs of sets such that, for every $i\in[m]$, $|A_i|=a\leq|B_i|=b$. Suppose that, for some $t\geq 0$,

$$
|A_i\cap A_j|\geq t\quad\text{for all }1\leq i,j\leq m,
$$

$$
|A_i\cap B_i|=0\quad\text{for all }1\leq i\leq m,
$$

$$
|A_i\cap B_j|>0\quad\text{for all }1\leq i\neq j\leq m.
$$

**Gerbner et al.'s conjecture.** Then

$$
m\leq AK(a+b,a,t).
$$

The conjecture is presented as a further research problem after the paper settles another conjecture of Gerbner et al. Its resolution is not stated in the supplied text.
technical_reason: For all equal-size set-pairs with t-intersecting A-family and cross-intersections, source Conjecture 4.1 asks AK(a+b,a,t). Its concluding paragraph explicitly reports Scott–Wilmer's proof using interior products. Source Theorem 1.5 has stronger cross-t hypotheses and is not itself a bridge. No investment; external proof body not fetched or independently audited.
quantifier_review: Full literal statement and quantifiers reviewed individually; precise caveats in technical_reason.

title: The rank-two conjecture for homologically trivial finite group actions on 4-manifolds
literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a closed orientable $4$-manifold with Euler characteristic $(M) \neq 0$, and let $G$ be a finite group acting effectively, locally linearly, and homologically trivially on $M$. Here $\operatorname{rank}_p(G)$ denotes the maximum rank of an elementary abelian $p$-subgroup of $G$. **Rank-two conjecture.** For every odd prime $p$,

$$
\operatorname{rank}_p(G) \leq 2.
$$

This conjecture proposes a uniform rank restriction for homologically trivial finite group actions on arbitrary closed orientable $4$-manifolds with nonzero Euler characteristic; it is compared in the source with an earlier conjecture of Edmonds. No resolution is indicated in the supplied text.
technical_reason: Every odd p and every effective locally linear homologically trivial action on a closed orientable four-manifold of nonzero Euler characteristic. Remark 1.1 supplies the fixed-point case; nonzero Euler characteristic alone is not a global-fixed-point argument. Spectral-sequence/topological obstruction remains; no small admissible action survives as concrete counterexample route.
quantifier_review: Full literal statement and quantifiers reviewed individually; precise caveats in technical_reason.

title: The characterization of 1-connected compact metric spaces by snowflake kernels
literal_statement:
Let $4\mathcal{M}^14$ denote the collection of all $1$-connected compact metric spaces, and let $4\mathfrak{S}_p4$ be the operator whose kernel consists of the spaces mapped to the zero space under the $p$-metric construction. Then **the characterization conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{M}^1=\mathop{\bigcap}_{p>1}\ker(\mathfrak{S}_p).
$$

The preceding results establish strict inclusions among the kernels $4\ker(\mathfrak{S}_p)4$ for different values of $p$, but do not determine this intersection. The conjecture proposes that it is exactly the class of all $1$-connected compact metric spaces.
technical_reason: Equality of classes requires both implications for all compact metric spaces and every real p>1. Source Proposition 3.25 proves the forward inclusion using connected closed one-dimensional subsets; arbitrary compact spaces with all snowflake quotients trivial are the missing direction. Finite spaces cannot settle that direction; no concrete pathological compact construction qualified.

title: Unique nearest-point conjecture for the stochastic phylogenetic variety
literal_statement:
Let $T=12|34$, let $I$ and $\Omega$ be the parameter sets specified in the paper, and define

$$
P_{0}:=\varphi _{T}(k_{0},1,k_{0},1,m_{0}).
$$

For $(k_{0},m_{0})\in I\times\Omega$, consider the point

$$
\varphi _{T}(\tilde{x}(k_{0},m_{0}),1,\tilde{x}(k_{0},m_{0}),1,1)\in\mathcal{V}_{T}^{+}.
$$

**Unique nearest-point conjecture.** The distance from $P_{0}$ to $\mathcal{V}_{T}^{+}$ is

$$
d(P_{0},\mathcal{V}_{T}^{+})=d\bigl(P_{0},\varphi _{T}(\tilde{x}(k_{0},m_{0}),1,\tilde{x}(k_{0},m_{0}),1,1)\bigr),
$$

and this point is the unique point of $\mathcal{V}_{T}^{+}$ minimizing the distance to $P_{0}$. Although the local minimum has been established, the paper states that it cannot prove this global-minimum claim and presents it as suggested by evidence.
technical_reason: For every parameter pair in I times Omega the specified point must be the unique GLOBAL nearest point. Source Conjecture 6.4 and local-minimum context distinguish this from Theorem 6.6, which assumes the conjectural uniqueness. A semialgebraic certificate over the full two-parameter domain is needed, not local Hessians or sampled minimizers; exact boundary/dependency and successor qualification incomplete.

title: The subcubic star chromatic index conjecture
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\chi'_{st}(G)$ denote its star chromatic index, the minimum number of colors in a proper edge coloring with no two-colored path or cycle of length four. **Subcubic star chromatic index conjecture.** If $G$ has maximum degree at most $3$, then

$$
\chi'_{st}(G) \leq 6.
$$

The conjecture concerns a uniform bound for star edge colorings of subcubic graphs. The source notes that it is settled for cubic Halin graphs, but does not indicate a resolution for all subcubic graphs.
technical_reason: All subcubic graphs require a proper edge coloring with six colors and no bichromatic four-edge path/cycle. Source Conjecture 1.1 records seven-color and special-family bounds. A universal reduction/extension argument is absent; small satisfiable instances cannot prove the assertion and no concrete certified obstruction is available.

title: Farrokhi–Safa lower-bound conjecture for the number of commutativity degrees
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. For a group $X$, let $l_M(X)$ denote the maximum length of chains of subgroups of $X$, and let $\mathcal{D}(G)$ be the set of commutativity degrees of $G$.

**Farrokhi–Safa's weaker conjecture.** Every finite group $G$ satisfies

$$
|\mathcal{D}(G)|\geqslant l_M\left(\frac{G}{Z(G)}\right)+1.
$$

This is stated as a weaker version of the preceding conjecture, giving a lower bound for the number of distinct commutativity degrees in terms of the subgroup-chain length of the central quotient. It is presented without a resolution in the source.
technical_reason: All finite groups, D(G) means relative subgroup commutativity degrees, not ordinary single-group commuting probability. Source Conjecture 1.4 and Theorem 1.5 separate the general chain-length lower bound from classification when exactly five values occur. Enumerating a few small groups would not bridge arbitrary central quotients; no tractable family with an exact failure was identified.

title: Nisan–Szegedy's sensitivity conjecture for Boolean functions
literal_statement:
Let $f$ be a Boolean function. Write $s(f)$ for its sensitivity and $bs(f)$ for its block sensitivity, the maximum number of pairwise disjoint blocks of input variables whose simultaneous flips change the value of $f$.

**Nisan–Szegedy's sensitivity conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that, for every Boolean function $f$,

$$
bs(f)\leq s(f)^C.
$$

The conjecture asks whether sensitivity is polynomially related to the other standard complexity measures of Boolean functions. The supplied context says that Hao's result directly resolves it, so the conjecture is solved.
technical_reason: Huang arXiv1907.00847v2 Theorem 1.5 gives bs(f)<=s(f)^4 for every Boolean f, exactly the required absolute exponent C=4. Read all six pages, including recursive signed-cube matrix proof, interlacing, degree bridge and references. Gotsman–Linial and Tal results are cited dependencies, not independently replayed here. The database's own statement already says solved.

title: Field-independent minimum rank for extended cube graphs
literal_statement: Let $t$ be an integer satisfying $t\equiv 0,1,2\pmod{6}$, and let $r$ be an integer with $r>\lfloor t/6\rfloor$. The **extended cube graphs** are denoted by $\operatorname{ECG}(t,6r-t-4)$. **Extended-cube conjecture.** These graphs have field-independent minimum rank, and their adjacency matrices are universally optimal. This conjecture is proposed as a possible characterization of the extended cube graphs for which maximum nullity equals the zero forcing number over an arbitrary field; equality does not hold for all extended cube graphs, and the conjectured field-independence and universal optimality remain unresolved in the supplied text.
technical_reason: Every admissible t congruent to 0,1,2 mod6 and every r>floor(t/6), over ALL fields. Source Conjecture 7.1 separates the symmetric ECG(6q+1,6q+1) theorem from general unequal parameters. Finite-field rank tests cannot prove universal field-optimality; graph-domain and zero-forcing transfer for asymmetric cases remain unqualified.

title: Conjecture on the maximum of Q for signature parameter r_2=1 in degree five
literal_statement:
Let $Q(5,1,\{4\},(x,y,1,g))$ be the function obtained after reducing to $z=1$ and $g\neq\pm1$, and let $(x,y,z,g)$ denote its parameters. **Maximum-value conjecture.** The maximum of $Q(5,1,\{4\},(x,y,1,g))$ is $16.6965\ldots$ and is attained at

$$
(x,y,z,g)=\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}},-1,1,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{7}}\right).
$$

This is a numerical conjecture about the optimization of the regulator-related function $Q$; the source provides no proof or resolution.

The restricted configuration lies within the successor's global ordered-root domain; published equality attains it. title: Conjectured maximizing points for M(n,1)
literal_statement:
Let $M(n,1)$ denote the maximum value of the regulator-related function for $r_2=1$, and let $C(1)$ be the corresponding threshold. **Maximizer conjecture for $r_2=1$.** One has $C(1)=4$, and for every $n\geq C(1)$, after a suitable change of variables, the maximum value $M(n,1)$ is attained at

$$
(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-3},x_{n-2},g)=(-1,0,-1,0,\ldots,-1,0)
$$

for even $n$, and at

$$
(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-3},x_{n-2},g)=\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}},-1,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}},-1,\ldots,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}},-1,1,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{7}}\right)
$$

for odd $n$. This predicts the maximizing configurations in the $r_2=1$ case; the source gives no proof or resolution.
technical_reason: All n>=4, both parity patterns and exact threshold C(1)=4. The same successor discusses iterative conjecture and proves low-degree cases, not an all-n maximizer theorem in the passages read. An isolated n=5 case cannot resolve this universal claim, and no uniform factorization/dominance induction was qualified.

title: The generating-level bound for the Hodge filtration of a free divisor
literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a complex manifold, let $D$ be a divisor satisfying the assumptions of Theorem and Corollary, and let $b_D(s)$ be the relevant Bernstein–Sato polynomial. For a well-filtered module $(\mathcal{M},F_\bullet)$, the filtration is **generated at level** $k$ when

$$
F_l\mathcal{D}_X\cdot F_k\mathcal{M}=F_{k+l}\mathcal{M}
$$

for every $l\geq 0$; its generating level is the smallest such integer. **Generating-level conjecture.** The Hodge filtration $F^H_\bullet\mathcal{O}_X(*D)$ is generated at level

$$
r:=\frac{1}{2}\left(\deg(b_D(s))-\operatorname{mult}_{b_D(s)}(-1)\right).
$$

This conjecture gives a bound for the complexity of the Hodge filtration and is supported by the calculations in the paper. Its general validity under the stated assumptions is not established here.
technical_reason: For every divisor satisfying the source's special freeness/comparison hypotheses, all filtration steps l>=0 must be generated at the prescribed Bernstein–Sato level. Selected introduction discusses root multiplicities and Conjecture4.12; exact hypothesis list and D-module dependencies not fully audited. A computed divisor example or lower generation level alone is insufficient to refute an upper generation bound.

title: Bonamy–Bousquet's conjecture on color savings for graph powers
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, let $k\geqslant 2$, and let $G^k$ denote its $k$-th power. Write $f(k,\Delta)$ for the corresponding upper-bound function on the number of colors.

**Bonamy–Bousquet's conjecture.** For every $k\geqslant 2$, only finitely many graphs $G$ satisfy

$$
\chi(G^k)\geqslant f(k,\Delta)+1-k.
$$

This conjecture proposes that, apart from finitely many exceptional graphs for each $k$, one can spare $k$ colors from the naive upper bound for coloring graph powers. It strengthens the known result that for $k\geqslant 3$, $\chi(G^k)\leqslant f(k,\Delta)-1$.
technical_reason: For each k>=2, finiteness over graphs with variable maximum degree requires the paper's graph conventions and f(k,Delta), not only a fixed-Delta theorem. Source Theorem7 only proves finiteness with gap<k-2 and Delta>=3. Low-degree/disconnected literal loopholes are scope corrections, not credit. No full universal sparing-k route qualified.

title: Bang–Koolen's classification conjecture for geometric distance-regular graphs
literal_statement:
Let $m\geq 2$ be a fixed integer. A **geometric distance-regular graph** is a distance-regular graph admitting a geometric structure, and let $\mu$ denote its intersection parameter and $-m$ its smallest eigenvalue. Assume the graph has diameter at least $3$.

**Bang–Koolen's classification conjecture.** Any such graph is a Johnson graph, a Hamming graph, a Grassmann graph, a bilinear forms graph, or has a number of vertices bounded by a function of $m$.

This conjecture proposes that, for fixed smallest eigenvalue and $\mu\geq 2$, the listed classical families account for all sufficiently large geometric distance-regular graphs. The paper proves classification results under additional hypotheses, while the general statement remains open.
technical_reason: For each fixed m>=2, all sufficiently large geometric distance-regular graphs with diameter>=3 AND mu>=2 must be one of four families. Source Conjecture1.7 contains mu>=2, only in the database's explanatory paragraph. Theorems characterizing special Johnson/Hamming cases do not cover all intersection arrays; omitted-hypothesis variants earn no credit.

title: Continuous broadcast-domination density conjecture in the plane
literal_statement:
Let a set of towers $\mathcal{T}\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be $(t,r)$-broadcasting if every point $v\in\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfies

$$
\sum_{T\in\mathcal{T}}\max\{t-d(T,v),0\}\geq r,
$$

where $d$ is the $\ell_1$ distance. Let $\delta'_{t,r}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ be the smallest upper density of a $(t,r)$-broadcasting set. **Continuous broadcast-domination conjecture.** There exists $\gamma_0>0$ such that, for all $\gamma\leq\gamma_0$,

$$
\delta'_{1,\gamma}(\mathbb{R}^2)=\lim_{\epsilon\to 0}\delta'_{1-\gamma/2,\epsilon}(\mathbb{R}^2)=\frac{1}{4(1-\frac{\gamma}{2})^2}.
$$

This is the continuous analogue of the paper's discrete conjecture and uses the $\ell_1$ metric to remain close to the grid setting. The claim is presented as a proposed direction, with no resolution given in the supplied text.
technical_reason: Existence of gamma0 followed by every sufficiently small positive gamma requires a sharp density LOWER bound for arbitrary tower configurations, not just the displayed lattice upper construction. Source Conjecture12 and the lattice determinant computation make this distinction explicit. Nonpositive-gamma wording and scaling corrections are uncredited; no global discharging certificate qualified.

title: Upper bound conjecture for total vertex product irregularity strength
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph of order $n$, and let $tvps(G)$ denote its total vertex product irregularity strength, namely the least integer $k$ for which $G$ has a product-irregular total labeling using labels from $\{1,\ldots,k\}$. **Upper bound conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that for every $d$-regular graph $G$ of order $n$

$$
tvps(G)\leq cn^{1/(d+1)}\ln{n}.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the logarithmic factor in the known upper bounds is sufficient for the existence of a product-irregular labeling of every regular graph. The paper establishes bounds of this general order for regular graphs, but the exact value of $tvps(G)$ remains open.
technical_reason: One absolute c must work simultaneously for every regular degree d and order n, with total vertex/edge labels in [k] and all vertex products distinct. Source Conjecture6.3 is stronger than separate degree-dependent bounds. A local-lemma route would need anti-concentration uniform in d with shared edge variables; no such full-scope estimate established. Trivial n=1/log endpoint is a domain defect, not discovery.

title: Conjecture on starting-vertex variability of the nearest unvisited vertex walk
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph, let $V$ be a uniformly random initial vertex, and let $L_{NUV}(G,V)$ denote the length of the nearest unvisited vertex walk started at $V$. Write ${\rm s.d.}(L_{NUV}(G,V))$ for its standard deviation and $\mathbb{E}L_{NUV}(G,V)$ for its expectation. **Starting-vertex variability conjecture.** The ratio

$$
\frac{ {\rm s.d.}(L_{NUV}(G,V))}{\mathbb{E} L_{NUV}(G,V)}
$$

is bounded over all finite graphs. This asks whether the variability caused by choosing the initial vertex uniformly is uniformly controlled, modifying the preceding question about the ratio of the maximum and minimum walk lengths; no resolution is given.
technical_reason: Uniform coefficient-of-variation bound over all finite weighted graph metrics and uniform starting vertices. Source Conjecture5 modifies the maximum/minimum question and discusses exponential random edge lengths separately. Tie-breaking/connectedness conventions matter; one anomalous start does not yield large variance without sufficient probability. No scalable metric family with proved NUV trajectories qualified.

title: Strong Fractional Tuza's conjecture
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\nu(G)$ be the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles in $G$. For $k\in\mathbb{N}$, a $k$-multi-transversal is a multiset $F\subseteq E(G)$ such that every triangle of $G$ contains at least $k$ elements of $F$. Define $\tau^*_k(G)$ to be the minimum of $|F|/k$ over all $k$-multi-transversals $F$.

**Strong Fractional Tuza's conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ with $k\geq 2$ and every graph $G$, 
$$
\tau^*_k(G)\leq 2\nu(G).
$$

This strengthens the fractional inequality $\tau^*(G)\leq 2\nu(G)$ by requiring a bounded-denominator multi-transversal for every $k\geq2$. The fractional inequality is known, but the stated uniform bound for all such $k$ is posed as an open question.
technical_reason: Source itself states Theorem2 for every integer k>=2 and every graph G, exactly tau_k^*<=2nu. Charging proofs for denominator3 and denominator2 are followed by combination to general k; selected construction/analysis passages read. No new argument warranted; long case-analysis appendices and all structural lemmas not independently audited.

title: Evasiveness conjecture for monotone transitive Boolean functions
literal_statement: A **Boolean function** is a function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$. Its decision-tree complexity $D(f)$ is the minimum number of input bits an adaptive algorithm must query to determine $f$, and $f$ is **evasive** when $D(f)=n$. The function is **monotone** if $f(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\leq f(y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ whenever $x_i\leq y_i$ for every $i$, and **transitive** if its symmetry group acts transitively on the coordinates. **Evasiveness conjecture.** Every non-constant monotone, transitive Boolean function is evasive.
technical_reason: Every nonconstant monotone coordinate-transitive Boolean function, with exact D(f)=n. Source proves almost-all monotone evasiveness in its random-complex setting, which does not imply every transitive function. Topological non-collapsibility/decision-tree lower bounds remain; a finite table would only cover instances.

title: The n-tree energy estimate for positive measures
literal_statement:
Let $T^n$ be the $n$-tree, let $\mu$ be a positive measure on $T^n$, let $\delta>0$, and let $\mathbf{V}_{\delta}^{\mu}$ and $\mathcal{E}[\mu]$ denote the associated truncated potential and energy. **The n-tree energy estimate.** For every positive integer $n$, there is a constant $C_n$ such that

$$
\int \mathbf{V}_{\delta}^{\mu}\,\mathrm{d}\mu\leq C_n(\delta|\mu|)^{\frac{2}{n+1}}\mathcal{E}[\mu]^{\frac{n-1}{n+1}}.
$$

This estimate is presented as a consequence of the surrogate maximum principle and is established in the paper for $n=1,2,3$; its assertion for all positive integers remains open.
technical_reason: For every n exists C_n uniform in positive measure and delta>0. Source Conjectures4.22/4.24 and conditional Lemma4.23 distinguish proved n<=3 from arbitrary products of trees. Substituting kappa=1/n presupposes the missing surrogate maximum principle; no valid dimension induction or exact positive-measure failure established.

title: Strong Coloring Conjecture for the strong chromatic number
literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a graph, let $Delta(H)$ denote its maximum degree, and let $schi(H)$ denote its strong chromatic number, the minimum number of colors needed so that every graph formed by adding a clique to the neighborhood of each vertex is properly colorable with those colors. **Strong Coloring Conjecture.** For any graph $H$, 

$$
s\chi(H)\leq 2\Delta(H).
$$

The bound would be best possible, since for each maximum degree $\Delta$ there are $\Delta$-regular graphs with strong chromatic number at least $2\Delta$. The conjecture remains open for all $\Delta\geq 2$, although several partial results are known for general $\Delta$.
technical_reason: All graphs under the actual strong coloring partition/transversal definition. The database's neighborhood-clique description is not that definition. Source Conjecture1.5 and partial ISR results do not prove the all-Delta bound; Delta=0 and literal gloss counterexamples earn no credit. No full strong-coloring mechanism qualified.

title: Capacity characterization for the Poisson channel with increasing power
literal_statement:
Consider the Poisson channel

$$
x[t] \geq 0 \quad \longrightarrow \quad y[t] \sim \operatorname{Pois}(x[t]),
$$

with power constraint $\tfrac{1}{n}\sum_{t=1}^n x[t] \leq n^\alpha$. This is the **Poisson channel with increasing power (PCIP)**. A normalized rate $\rho>0$ is achievable if, for every $\epsilon>0$, one can design a code for some blocklength $n$ with error probability at most $\epsilon$ and rate $\rho\log n$; let $\bar C(\alpha)$ be the closure of achievable normalized rates. **PCIP capacity conjecture.** For the PCIP, $\bar C(\alpha)=\alpha/2$. This characterizes the maximum achievable normalized rate when the power constraint grows polynomially with the blocklength; the supplied text does not establish the claim's resolution.
technical_reason: All alpha and every epsilon with normalized rho log n coding rates require the genuine increasing-power Poisson channel definition. The cited arXiv2001.06311 retained body concerns DNA noisy shuffling/sampling capacity, not the displayed PCIP conjecture in the inspected theorem sections. Wrong-source correction is uncredited; no capacity proof or primary scope qualification claimed.

title: Minimum-weight codeword conjecture for degree-4 maximal arcs
literal_statement: Let $D$ be a design associated with a maximal arc of degree $4$ in $PG(2,2^m)$, where $m\ge 2$, and let $A$ be its incidence matrix. Let $C$ be the binary code spanned by the rows of $A$. **Minimum-weight codeword conjecture.** The code $C$ has minimum distance $4$, and every codeword of minimum weight is a row of $A$. This conjecture arises from computations with resolvable $2$-$(52,4,1)$ designs associated with maximal arcs in projective planes of order $16$; its validity in general is not established by the supplied text.

Source Conjecture3.1 separates Desarguesian arcs from extra minimum words in other order16 planes. Those other-plane examples are inadmissible counterexamples. title: The 2n/3 minimum semi-degree conjecture for directed W-cycle-factors
literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph of order $n$, let $W\subseteq V(D)$, and let

$$
|W|=n_1+\cdots+n_k,
$$

where each $n_i\geq 3$. An **arbitrary $W$-cycle-factor** is a collection of $k$ disjoint directed cycles $C_1,\ldots,C_k$ such that $|V(C_i)\cap W|=n_i$ for every $i$.

**The $2n/3$ minimum semi-degree conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^0(W)\geq 2n/3,
$$

then $D$ contains an arbitrary $W$-cycle-factor.

The conjecture improves the paper's proved $(3n-3)/4$ minimum semi-degree condition when all prescribed parts have size at least $3$. The source gives a sharpness example below the proposed threshold but does not report a resolution.
technical_reason: Every digraph/order/W partition with all prescribed n_i>=3 and semidegree>=2n/3. The source explains this would imply disjoint directed triangle-factor conjectures. Its sharpness example lies below threshold; transplanting it is invalid. No above-threshold obstruction or universal prescribed-intersection cycle decomposition obtained.

title: Minimum diameter conjecture for flip graphs of 3-dimensional polytopes
literal_statement:
Let $P$ range over all $3$-dimensional polytopes with $n$ vertices, and let $f$ range over all generic linear functionals on $P$. Write $G(P,f)$ for the flip graph associated with the monotone structure induced by $f$. **Minimum diameter conjecture.** The minimum diameter of $G(P,f)$ is

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{n+5}{4}\right\rfloor
$$

for every $n\geq 4$. This minimum can be achieved by simple polytopes for every even $n$. The conjecture concerns the expected lower bound for flip-graph diameters in dimension three; the source presents it as an open problem.
technical_reason: Minimum over ALL 3-polytopes and generic functionals equals floor((n+5)/4), every n>=4. Source Conjecture6.1 distinguishes extremal simple-polytope attainment at even n from a universal diameter lower bound. Computing a few oriented polytopes cannot prove the min bound; no concrete lower-diameter candidate or full reduction qualified.

title: Reiher–LPR extremal function conjecture for triangle-free graphs
literal_statement:
For integers $n$ and $s$ with $n/3<s\le n/2$, let $\mathrm{ex}(n,s)$ be the largest number of edges in a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices whose independence number is at most $s$. For every $k\ge1$, define

$$
g_k(n,s)=\frac{k(k-1)n^2}{2}-k(3k-4)ns+\frac{(3k-4)(3k-1)s^2}{2}.
$$

**Reiher–LPR conjecture.** One has

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,s)=\min_k g_k(n,s).
$$

This refines Andrásfai's piecewise-quadratic prediction. The paper proves the formula in a neighbourhood to the right of each critical ratio, while the asserted formula over the full range remains open.
technical_reason: Every integer pair n/3<s<=n/2 with minimum over ALL k>=1, not only local critical-ratio intervals. Source Theorems1.2/1.3 prove near-threshold or high-minimum-degree cases. Blow-up constructions give candidate lower bounds but no general extremal upper bound; no integer-rounding failure established.

title: Embedding conjecture for optimal dimension-four binary codes
literal_statement: Let $[n,4]$ codes be binary linear codes of length $n$ and dimension $4$. A code is **optimal** if its minimum distance is $d(n,4)$, and it is **self-orthogonal** if it is orthogonal to itself. title: The unimodality conjecture for the function beta

title: The threshold conjecture for biased Maker–Breaker $H$-factor games

Let $b_\Delta$ denote the threshold bias for the biased Maker–Breaker $H$-factor game, where $H$ has maximum degree $\Delta$. **Threshold conjecture.** For all $\Delta \ge 3$,

b_\Delta = \Theta(n^{2/(\Delta + 3)}).

title: Integer-power conjecture for forbidden-subgraph planar counts
literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite set of graphs, let $H$ be a graph, and let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,H,\mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex planar graph containing no graph in $\mathcal{F}$ as a subgraph.

**Integer-power conjecture.** For all finite sets of graphs $\mathcal{F}$ and all graphs $H$, there is an integer $k$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,H,\mathcal{F})=\Theta(n^k).
$$

This generalizes the preceding planar conjecture to forbidden subgraphs. The paper poses it as open; its precise scope includes arbitrary finite forbidden families and arbitrary graphs being counted.

title: Conjectured sharp upper bounds for induced degenerate subgraphs of planar graphs

$$
\bar\alpha_2=2/3,\qquad \bar\alpha_3=5/6,\qquad \bar\alpha_4=11/12.

title: Stahl's conjecture on multichromatic numbers of Kneser graphs
literal_statement:
Let $k$, $d$, and $s$ be integers with $d\geq 2s$. The $k$th multichromatic number $\chi_k(G)$ is the smallest number of colors needed to assign each vertex of a graph $G$ a set of $k$ colors so that adjacent vertices receive disjoint sets. The Kneser graph $K(d,s)$ has as vertices the $s$-subsets of $[d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}$, with two vertices adjacent when the corresponding sets are disjoint.

**Stahl's conjecture.** For all integers $k$ and $d\geq 2s$,

$$
\chi_k(K(d,s))=\left\lceil\frac{k}{s}\right\rceil\cdot(d-2s)+2k.
$$

This conjecture concerns the multichromatic numbers of Kneser graphs and has applications to hardness results for graph coloring and orthogonality dimension. More than forty years after it was proposed, it remains open.

title: Fifth-order differential equation conjecture for the degree-of-symmetry generating function of Dyck paths

title: The bounded-decoration conjecture for hypergraphs
literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a hypergraph, meaning a family of subsets of a finite set $V$. Assign a real number $f(v)$ to each $v\in V$, and write

$$
S(A)=\sum_{x\in A}f(x)
$$

for $A\in\mathcal F$. The decoration is **cool** if $S(A)\ne S(B)$ whenever $A$ and $B$ have non-empty intersection. **The bounded-decoration conjecture.** For every $\Delta$ there is a constant $C=C(\Delta)$ such that every hypergraph $\mathcal F$ of maximum degree $\Delta$ has a cool decoration from the set $\{1,2,\dots,C\}$. title: The $P_{4k-4}$ Cartesian-product non-Hamiltonicity conjecture

title: The dichotomy conjecture for induced poset saturation
literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a poset, let $B_n$ be the Boolean lattice on $[n]$, and let ${\rm sat}^*(n,P)$ denote the minimum size of a maximal induced $P$-free subposet of $B_n$.

**Induced saturation dichotomy conjecture.** Either there exists a constant $K_P$ such that

$$
{\rm sat}^*(n,P)\le K_P,
$$

or, for every $n$,

$$
{\rm sat}^*(n,P)\ge n+1.
$$

This strengthens the paper's dichotomy theorem, which gives the weaker alternative lower bound ${\rm sat}^*(n,P)\ge\log_2 n$ in the unbounded case. The proposed linear lower bound remains open.

title: Mynhardt–Roux path and cycle non-realisation conjecture for irredundance graphs

**Mynhardt–Roux's conjecture.** For every $n\geq3$, $P_n$ is not an $\operatorname{IR}$-graph, and for every $n\geq5$, $C_n$ is not an $\operatorname{IR}$-graph.

title: Beaton–Bouvel–Guerrini–Rinaldi's right-to-left-minimum refinement for 2314-avoiding permutations

$$
c_{1,1}=1,\qquad c_{n,0}=0,
$$

for $n\geq1$, and

$$
c_{n,k}=c_{n-1,k-1}+k\sum_{j=k}^{n-1}c_{n-1,j}
$$

for $n\geq2$ and $1\leq k\leq n$. A right-to-left minimum of a permutation is an entry smaller than every entry to its right.
**Beaton–Bouvel–Guerrini–Rinaldi's refinement conjecture.** The number of permutations in $cmathfrak{S}_n(\underline{23}14)$ with $k$ right-to-left minima is $c_{n,k}$.

title: Rainbow saturation conjecture for uniform hypergraphs
literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph, and let ${\operatorname{sat}^\star}_k(n,H)$ denote the minimum number of hyperedges in an $n$-vertex rainbow $H$-saturated $k$-uniform hypergraph.

**Rainbow hypergraph saturation conjecture.** For every $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$, we have

$$
{\operatorname{sat}^\star}_k(n,H)=O(n^{k-1}).
$$

This conjecture is the rainbow analogue of Pikhurko's bound for ordinary saturation in uniform hypergraphs. title: The simultaneous clique-maximisation conjecture for graphs on surfaces
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph embeddable in a surface $\Sigma$. Let $C(G)$ denote its total number of complete subgraphs, let $C(\Sigma,n)$ be the maximum of $C(G)$ over all such graphs, and let $C(K_s,\Sigma,n)$ be the maximum number of copies of $K_s$ in an $n$-vertex graph embeddable in $\Sigma$.

**Simultaneous clique-maximisation conjecture.** If $C(G)=C(\Sigma,n)$, then for every $s\geqslant 0$,

$$
C(K_s,G) = C(K_s,\Sigma,n).
$$

This is the equality-case counterpart of the clique-count decomposition conjecture: every graph attaining the maximum total clique count should also attain each individual clique-count maximum. It has been verified for the surfaces listed in the paper, while the assertion for arbitrary surfaces remains open.

title: Conjecture on bounded-degree induced trees in random graphs
literal_statement:
Let $G_{n,p}$ be the binomial random graph. For a graph $G$, write $T(G)$ for the size of a largest induced subtree, and set $q=(1-p)^{-1}$. Let $\Delta\geq 2$ be an integer and let $p=p(n)$ satisfy

$$
\frac{C}{n}<p<0.99,
$$

where $C=C(\Delta)$ is a sufficiently large constant depending only on $\Delta$. Let $T$ be a tree with

$$
b=(1-o(1))2\log_q(np)
$$

vertices and maximum degree $\Delta$. **Bounded-degree induced-tree conjecture.** With high probability, $G_{n,p}$ contains $T$ as an induced subgraph. The paper proves this when $n^{-1/2}\ln^{10/9}n\leq p\leq 0.99$ and leaves the smaller-$p$ range open.

title: The extremal-function formulation of Frankl's conjecture
literal_statement:
For $a,n\in\mathbb{N}^+$, let $\mathcal{S}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ be a union-closed family such that every element of $[n]$ belongs to at most $a$ sets of $\mathcal{S}$. Let $f(n,a)$ denote the maximum possible cardinality of such a family.

**Extremal formulation of Frankl's conjecture.** For every $a,n\in\mathbb{N}^+$,

$$
|\mathcal{S}|\leq 2a.
$$

Equivalently, $f(n,a)\leq 2a$ for all $a,n\in\mathbb{N}^+$. This formulation is stated as equivalent to Frankl's conjecture and is the starting point for the paper's linear-relaxation bounds, but it remains open in general.

title: Quadratic discrepancy conjecture for the Pref-opposite construction

A **de Bruijn sequence** of order $n$ is a cyclic binary sequence in which every binary word of length $n$ occurs exactly once; the **Pref-opposite** algorithm is the construction specified in the source. title: Maximum discrepancy conjecture for the de Bruijn sequence DB_max

title: The minimum Graovac-Ghorbani index conjecture for the B2 family

title: De Caen–Erdős–Pullman–Wormald clique-partition conjecture
literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}_n$ be the set of all graphs on $n$ vertices, let $\overline{G}$ denote the complement of a graph $G$, and let $\operatorname{cp}(G)$ be the minimum number of cliques whose edge sets partition the edges of $G$. Define

$$
M_n=\max_{G\in\mathcal{G}_n}\left(\operatorname{cp}(G)+\operatorname{cp}(\overline{G})\right).
$$

**De Caen–Erdős–Pullman–Wormald conjecture.**

$$
M_n\sim\frac{7}{25}n^2.
$$

The known bounds are $\frac{7n^2}{25}+O(n)\leq M_n\leq\frac{13n^2}{30}+O(n)$. Thus the conjecture asserts that the lower bound is asymptotically tight, while closing this gap remains open.

title: Petty's conjecture on equilateral sets in normed spaces
literal_statement:
Let $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ be a normed space of dimension $n$. A set $S\subseteq X$ is **equilateral** if there is a constant $c>0$ such that $\|x-y\|=c$ for all distinct $x,y\in S$, and let $e(X)$ denote the largest cardinality of an equilateral set in $X$.

**Petty's conjecture.** For all normed spaces $X$ of dimension $n$, 

$$
e(X)\geq n+1.
$$

The conjecture gives a general lower bound for equilateral sets in finite-dimensional normed spaces. It is known in dimension at most four, while for $n\geq 5$ it remains open except for some special classes of norms.

title: Bounded-degree Cayley graphs without a bounded eigenbasis
literal_statement:
A Cayley graph is a graph whose vertices form a group and whose edges are invariant under the group's regular action; an eigenbasis of its adjacency matrix is **$C$-bounded** if every eigenfunction in the basis satisfies $\lVert x\rVert_{L^\infty}\leq C\lVert x\rVert_{L^2}$.

**Bounded-degree eigenbasis conjecture.** There exists some $d$ such that for every $C$ there exists a $d$-regular Cayley graph without an orthonormal $C$-bounded eigenbasis.

The preceding results establish lower and upper bounds for the smallest possible eigenbasis bound, but the lower-bound construction uses graphs of increasing degree. This conjecture asks whether bounded-degree Cayley graphs can also lack a bounded eigenbasis; its status is presented as unknown.

Source Conjecture1.5 distinguishes growing-degree constructions and bounded irreducible-dimension positive cases. title: Brešar, Klavžar, Rall, and Wash's packing chromatic number conjecture for subdivisions of subcubic graphs
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic graph, and let $D(G)$ denote its subdivision, obtained by replacing each edge of $G$ by a path of length two. The **packing chromatic number** $\chi_p(G)$ is the minimum $k$ for which $G$ has a packing $(1,2,\ldots,k)$-coloring, where a packing $(s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k)$-coloring partitions the vertex set into classes $V_1,V_2,\ldots,V_k$ such that the distance between distinct vertices in $V_i$ is at least $s_i+1$. **Brešar, Klavžar, Rall, and Wash's conjecture.** The subdivision satisfies

$$
\chi_p(D(G))\leq 5.
$$

This conjecture concerns whether the packing chromatic number is uniformly bounded for subdivisions of subcubic graphs; the source presents it as a conjecture following an earlier question by Gastineau and Togni, and does not state a resolution.
